html:
SMTO-SLM-0003 — The SLURM settings files go too deep or loop back

GUID: 3ea21b14-19e8-4f2e-b16b-a25082fe1e0c
Slug: slurm-config-limit
Domain: SLM · Subsystem: slm

What happened

  • The cluster's settings file pulls in too many other files, or the files point back to each other in a loop. Your SLURM command still runs, but SMTO won't remember this cluster for the conversation.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask the administrator to check the Include lines in slurm.conf on the Gateway computer and make sure no file is included twice or includes a file that leads back to it. A loop of settings files has no end, so SMTO stops reading.
  2. Ask them to check for shortcuts (symbolic links) among those files that point back to each other. Shortcuts that point in a circle create the same loop.
  3. Ask them whether the settings could use fewer nested files: no more than 16 in total and no more than 4 levels deep. SMTO reads only a limited number of settings files so it never gets stuck.
  4. After a fix, ask the Agent to run sinfo on that Gateway. A successful simple SLURM read lets SMTO recognise the cluster again.

What success looks like

  • The Agent runs sinfo or squeue on that Gateway without this error.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the SLURM cluster or SMTO. Don't ask anyone to turn off SMTO's reading limits; fix the loop or trim the files instead.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • SLURM configuration discovery stopped because the include tree exceeded its limits (more than 4 include levels, 16 files, 512 KiB total or 1,024-byte paths), a symlink loop was found, or a file was included twice.

What this means

  • Config/include traversal exceeds depth/file/path bounds, symlink resolution detects a loop, or an already-seen real configuration path is revisited. These checks describe local configuration identity and continuity eligibility. They do not query cluster health or prove command rollback; execution and optional observation evidence remain distinct.

Why this can happen

  • Config/include traversal exceeds depth/file/path bounds, symlink resolution detects a loop, or an already-seen real configuration path is revisited.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect include and symlink relationships against the bounded traversal without widening safety limits.

How to fix it

  • On the Gateway host, follow the Include lines and symlinks from SLURM_CONF or /etc/slurm/slurm.conf: remove cycles and duplicate includes, and keep the tree within 4 levels, 16 .conf files, 512 KiB and 1,024-byte paths. Do not raise or disable the discovery limits; change the real configuration only if it is actually wrong.
  • Inspect include and symlink targets. Remove unintended cycles or select a bounded supported configuration; do not disable discovery safety limits.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • An intended bounded acyclic configuration tree can be observed.

What not to do

  • Do not bypass scope or ownership checks to force a larger operation through.

Technical notes

  • These checks describe local configuration identity and continuity eligibility. They do not query cluster health or prove command rollback; execution and optional observation evidence remain distinct.
